intro.caption: Lesson 2-4 — box plots. Max Maxwell locked Clip Squad inside an algorithm escape room! Every lock asks for the five-number summary.

balloons.t: Whoa! Max locked the studio door! Our stream viewers are waiting!
Three locks on this door. Each one wants pieces of a box plot!
Five-number summary, losers! Min, Q1, median, Q3, max. Bet you mess up the quartiles!
First lock gives 9 ordered view counts in thousands: 4, 7, 9, 12, 15, 18, 20, 24, 30.

pages.caption: A box plot is built from five key numbers: minimum, Q1, median, Q3, and maximum.

balloons.t: Start with the easiest three: the minimum, the median, and the maximum!
Easy! Keep the median 15 inside the lower half, right?
Stop! Leave OUT the single median! The lower half is just 4, 7, 9, 12!
Lock 3 draws the box plot! Remember what the box itself covers and what the whiskers reach.
The box holds the middle half. The whiskers stretch to the extremes!

pages.ch: Boss Gate · The Final Vault Lock

balloons.t: One last set: 10, 14, 18, 22, 28, 32, 40. Three final slots!
Do not include the median in the halves, and do not confuse Q1 with the minimum!
We're out! Max's escape room could not hold the Clip Squad!

win.caption: A box plot displays the five-number summary: minimum, Q1 (median of the lower half), median, Q3 (median of the upper half), and maximum. The box spans from Q1 to Q3 and holds the middle 50% of the data.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Min, Median, and Max
gates.prompt: Use the 9 ordered view counts (in thousands): 4, 7, 9, 12, 15, 18, 20, 24, 30.
hints: Conceptual: the minimum is the least value, the maximum is the greatest value, and the median is the middle of the ordered list.
Procedural: with 9 ordered values, the middle one is the 5th value.

steps: With 7 values, the 4th value is in the middle: Median = 11.

items.label: Median of 4, 7, 9, 12, 15, 18, 20, 24, 30:
items.aria: median of the nine view counts

fb.msg: 4 is the minimum, not the middle.
12 is the 4th value. With 9 values, the middle is the 5th.

items.fbDefault: Count in 5 spots from either end of the 9 ordered numbers.

options.fb: Those are inside the ends. Minimum is the very smallest; maximum is the very largest.
There is no 0 in the data set. Read from the actual values.

gates.pass: Click! Lock 1 opens: Min = 4, Median = 15, Max = 30.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Find Q1 and Q3
gates.prompt: Find Q1 and Q3 for 4, 7, 9, 12, 15, 18, 20, 24, 30. Remember: leave out the single median 15 when splitting into halves!
hints: Conceptual: Q1 is the median of the lower half, and Q3 is the median of the upper half — never the minimum or maximum.
Procedural: lower half is 4, 7, 9, 12 (average 7 and 9). Upper half is 18, 20, 24, 30 (average 20 and 24).

steps: Practice set (7 values): 2, 5, 9, [13], 17, 21, 29. Leave out the median 13.
Lower half is 2, 5, 9 → its middle is Q1 = 5.
Upper half is 17, 21, 29 → its middle is Q3 = 21.

items.label: Q1 (median of lower half 4, 7, 9, 12):

fb.msg: You included the median 15 in the lower half! Leave out 15, so the lower half is 4, 7, 9, 12.
4 is the minimum, not Q1. Q1 is the median of the lower half.
7 is only the 2nd value. Average the middle two of the lower half (7 and 9).

items.fbDefault: Average the two middle numbers of 4, 7, 9, 12.

items.label: Q3 (median of upper half 18, 20, 24, 30):

fb.msg: You included the median 15 in the upper half! Leave out 15, so the upper half is 18, 20, 24, 30.
30 is the maximum, not Q3. Q3 is the median of the upper half.

items.fbDefault: Average the two middle numbers of 18, 20, 24, 30.

gates.pass: Click! Lock 2 opens: Q1 = 8 and Q3 = 22.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Build the Box
gates.prompt: Your five-number summary is Min = 4, Q1 = 8, Median = 15, Q3 = 22, Max = 30. Read the box plot.
hints: Conceptual: the box holds the middle 50% of the data, and the whiskers reach out to the minimum and maximum.
Procedural: the left edge of the box is Q1, the right edge is Q3, and the line inside is the median.

steps: Suppose a box plot has Min = 1, Q1 = 6, Median = 10, Q3 = 16, Max = 25.
The box stretches from Q1 (6) to Q3 (16), holding the middle 50% of values.
The whiskers reach from 6 down to 1 and from 16 up to 25.
worked.q: In that practice plot, where does the right whisker end?

items.q: Which two values form the left and right edges of the BOX?

options.fb: 4 and 30 are the ends of the whiskers, not the box.
15 is the median line inside the box. The box stretches from Q1 to Q3.
4 is the minimum whisker tip. The box goes from Q1 (8) to Q3 (22).

items.q: What percent of the data sits inside the box (between Q1 = 8 and Q3 = 22)?

options.fb: 25% is just one quarter (like from Min to Q1). The box covers two quarters.
75% would cover three quarters. The box covers the middle half.
100% is from Min to Max, including both whiskers.

gates.pass: Click! Lock 3 opens — the box spans 8 to 22 and holds the middle 50%.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Open the Last Lock
gates.prompt: Crack the final vault using this 7-value data set: 10, 14, 18, 22, 28, 32, 40.
hints: Conceptual: leave out the single median (22) before finding Q1 and Q3, and never confuse Q1 with the minimum.
Procedural: lower half is 10, 14, 18; upper half is 28, 32, 40.

steps: Leave out 15. Q1 is the middle of 5, 9, 12 → 9.
Q3 is the middle of 19, 24, 31 → 24. The line inside the box sits at 15.

items.label: Lock 1 · Find Q1 of 10, 14, 18, 22, 28, 32, 40:
items.aria: Q1 of the final vault data

fb.msg: 10 is the minimum, not Q1. Q1 is the middle of the lower half (10, 14, 18).
Leave out the median 22 when finding the lower half: 10, 14, 18.

items.fbDefault: Find the middle number of the lower half: 10, 14, 18.

items.label: Lock 2 · Find Q3 of 10, 14, 18, 22, 28, 32, 40:
items.aria: Q3 of the final vault data

fb.msg: Leave out the median 22; the upper half is 28, 32, 40.

items.fbDefault: Find the middle number of the upper half: 28, 32, 40.

items.q: Lock 3 · In a box plot for 10, 14, 18, 22, 28, 32, 40, where does the line inside the box sit?

options.fb: 14 is the left edge of the box.
The line inside the box is the median (22), not the midpoint of min and max.

gates.pass: CLANG! Q1 = 14, Q3 = 32, Median = 22. The escape room door swings open!

journal.heading: Lesson 2-4 — what the escape room taught us
rows: Minimum, Q1, median, Q3, and maximum — the five values that build every box plot.
When an odd-count data set has one single middle number, exclude it before finding Q1 and Q3.
The minimum is the whisker tip; Q1 is the median of the lower half and starts the box.
The box stretches from Q1 to Q3 and always holds the middle half of the data.
journal.quote: "Leave the single median out when you split the halves, and the lock opens every time." — Mei

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 2-4 (Represent and Describe Data in a Box Plot) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: the five-number summary, excluding the single median when finding Q1/Q3, and interpreting the box and whiskers.
standards: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms, and box plots
